page: Microsoft Azure DS14-4_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical cores with 4 vCPUs, allocating a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 112.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 28.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance is provisioned with 229 GB of local storage and operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates a clear tradeoff between compute capability and memory performance. The instance exhibits weak CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are positioned in the lower percentile. However, memory subsystem performance is more robust, with cached read-only memory bandwidth reaching 359.24 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth at 32.61 GB/sec, both scoring in the average tier. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform in the average range, processing 6.03 million operations per second.

Given the high memory density relative to the limited compute resources, the DS14-4_v2 is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring large memory footprints but low CPU utilization. It is well-suited for in-memory caching, database operations, and lightweight data processing tasks. Conversely, it is poorly suited for compute-heavy applications, software compilation, or large-scale language model inference, as demonstrated by poor performance on 7B parameter models.
